open_questions.topic: Scope of this story vs. the full mapped page
open_questions.detail: The Figma frame captured is the entire Forno Rosso home page (header, hero, delivery banner, featured menu, story, footer), but the branch/story is named 'delivery-promise-banner' and node-id 6:40 in the source Figma URL is the delivery-banner section specifically. It is unclear whether this story should ship only the DeliveryPromiseBanner (node 6:40) dropped into an existing/otherwise-out-of-scope page shell, or whether the whole home page mapped here is in scope for this story.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Mapped every section of the page for layout context, but scoped the implementation recommendation to DeliveryPromiseBanner and its children (DeliveryHighlight, IconBadge, StatGroup, StatBlock) as the deliverable for THIS story; the other proposed components (SiteHeader, HeroSection, FeaturedMenuSection, StorySection, SiteFooter, etc.) are documented but treated as out-of-scope/future work unless the reviewer says otherwise.

options.label: Banner only — build DeliveryPromiseBanner (node 6:40) and its children; assume the rest of the page exists or is out of scope
Full page — build every section mapped here (header through footer) as part of this story

open_questions.topic: Long pizza names overflow the card title/price row
open_questions.detail: Two of the four PizzaCard titles ('Funghi Selvatici & Tartufo', 'Prosciutto Crudo e Rucola') are wider than the 262px title/price row and Figma itself renders them truncated with an ellipsis ('Funghi Selvatici &...', 'Prosciutto Crudo e...'), even though the full name is stored in the node's text content.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Implement the card title as single-line CSS text-overflow: ellipsis (matching what the design literally renders), with the full name available via a `title`/aria-label attribute for accessibility — not a wrapped two-line title.

open_questions.topic: Two distinct near-white section backgrounds with no semantic naming
open_questions.detail: featured-section shows the page's own background (#FCFAF6) while story-section paints an explicit, slightly different off-white (#F3EFE9). Both read as 'cream' but are different hex values with no token names distinguishing them in the source file.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Kept them as two separate tokens (`bg-page` #FCFAF6, `bg-story` #F3EFE9) to preserve the subtle section-to-section contrast visible in the render, rather than collapsing them into one value.

open_questions.topic: Hero eyebrow badge icon is named 'fire-extinguisher'
open_questions.detail: The icon inside the 'Authentic Neapolitan Woodfired' eyebrow badge (node 6:679) is named 'fire-extinguisher' in the Figma layer tree, which doesn't match the woodfired/flame messaging of the badge it sits in.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Treated this as a mislabeled icon-library pick and mapped it to a 'flame' icon (consistent with the surrounding copy), not a literal fire-extinguisher glyph.

open_questions.topic: Two different ETA figures on the same page
open_questions.detail: The header shows 'Estimated delivery: 30 mins' while the delivery-promise banner's StatBlock shows 'Average ETA: 25 - 35 Min'. These could be meant to be the same dynamic value or intentionally different (a live order estimate vs. a general marketing stat).
open_questions.arc_assumption: Modeled them as two independent static content fields (HeaderCartStatus.etaValue and StatBlock.value) rather than a single shared data source.

open_questions.topic: Frame is desktop-only (1440px), no mobile/tablet variant provided
open_questions.detail: Every section in this frame is authored at a fixed 1440px width (e.g. the 4-column PizzaCardGrid, the two-column hero and story sections). No narrower artboard or component variant exists in the source file to show how these reflow.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Assumed standard responsive stacking on implementation (e.g. PizzaCardGrid 4→2→1 columns, two-column sections stacking to one column) using the same tokens, without a designed reference to confirm exact breakpoints.

open_questions.topic: Footer social icons and legal links have no destination URLs
open_questions.detail: SocialIconButton (Instagram/Facebook/Twitter) and FooterLegalLinks (Privacy Policy, Delivery Terms) are drawn as icons/labels only; the Figma file carries no href/interaction data for any of them.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Wired them to placeholder `#` hrefs pending real destination URLs from the client/content team.

open_questions.topic: No empty-cart or post-click feedback state designed
open_questions.detail: CartButton always shows a hardcoded count of 3, and 'Add to Order' has no drawn hover/loading/added-confirmation state.
open_questions.arc_assumption: CartButton hides its count badge entirely when count is 0; ButtonDark ('Add to Order') gets only a generic hover/focus treatment derived from existing tokens, with no bespoke 'added' state, pending product input.
